clue.text: Go for prominent aristocrat

parts.note: a star is a leading, prominent figure, as in a star player
a toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class person

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and fetch a well-known nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for someone upper-class or posh.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off on a journey is simply to go, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Ulster party rejected god

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the pieces are written in the opposite direction

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often loosely called Ulster
a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish political party has turned its back on a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster party' looks like one political group, such as a unionist party, but the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor, is an example of a god.

clue.text: Rodent eating Sunday's dessert

indicators.note: one thing eating another holds it inside, so the rodent surrounds the day's letter

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent
S is a standard abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A mouse nibbling away at the pudding prepared for Sunday lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped chocolate or fruit pudding is a classic sweet course.

clue.text: Happen space traveller has regret

parts.note: a comet is a body that travels through space
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: An astronaut, maybe, feels remorse about something that occurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish or dream that is fulfilled is said to be realised; this idiom means to happen as hoped.

clue.text: Stimulant initially could blight the aristocracy

parts.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word could

parts.note: rust is a fungal blight of plants

explanation.surface: A warning that pep pills might ruin the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest social class, the nobility, is idiomatically called this, like the top layer of a pie.

clue.text: Ruler, for example, fills the breach

indicators.note: one piece filling another sits inside it, so the example abbreviation goes into the tear

parts.note: a rent is a tear or breach

explanation.surface: A monarch, say, steps into the gap in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: One who governs in place of an underage or absent monarch is a ruler.

clue.text: Boss promises to be hard-working

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: An employer pledges to be diligent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests an employer, but here it is a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligent scholar devoted to study is hard-working.

clue.text: April's novel corkscrew

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman named April has written a book about a corkscrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal on APRILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew shape is a helix or spiral, used here as a noun or adjective.

clue.text: Bird returns like this to quarry

indicators.note: returns means the word for like this comes back the other way

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
quarry is hunted prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey comes back in this way to its target.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-eating hawk is a large raptor, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Show amusement as Romeo is caught in a trap

indicators.note: something caught in a snare sits inside it, so the letter goes within the trap word

parts.note: a gin is a trap or snare for animals
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Laughing as a lover ends up ensnared.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad smile is a way to show amusement.

clue.text: Alcohol in science fiction always gives beastly sickness

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the genre abbreviation

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Drinking in sci-fi stories always ends in a nasty illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A viral influenza of pigs is literally a disease of beasts.

clue.text: Bob has to fasten item of clothing

parts.note: to bob is to bow or curtsy briefly
to tie is to fasten

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob must do up a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' reads as a man's name; it is the verb for a quick bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotted neck accessory worn with evening dress is an item of clothing.

clue.text: It isn't done to fabricate a complaint

indicators.note: to fabricate is to make up or construct, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: It is bad form to invent a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests a grievance, but it is a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of a tendon is a physical ailment, the medical sense of complaint.

clue.text: Change of rota has municipality in outrage

indicators.note: a change of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: a city is a municipality

explanation.surface: A new duty rota at the town hall causes fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked, shocking act is an outrage.

clue.text: Knight invested in gleaming decorations

indicators.note: to be invested in is to be clothed or put inside, so the chess letter goes within

parts.note: fiery means blazing or gleaming
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight dressed in shining ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy clothes and ornaments worn for display are decorations.

clue.text: A copper involved in roll in sports car

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the pair goes within the list word

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A police officer caught up in a list, perhaps a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: D stands for the old penny (denarius), a copper coin in pre-decimal Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An open two-seater car built for speed is a sports car.

clue.text: Take exception to Egyptian leader retiring

parts.note: to demur is to raise an objection

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word Egyptian

explanation.surface: Objecting to a pharaoh's stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests leaving office; it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and shy, a person who is reserved is retiring.

clue.text: Intensify destruction of a celesta

indicators.note: destruction breaks the letters up so they can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Smashing up a keyboard instrument makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: A celesta is a small keyboard instrument with chiming metal bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up or worsen a conflict is to intensify it.

clue.text: Gloomy king beset by wild animal

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the animal goes around the royal letter

parts.note: a moose is a large wild deer
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A sad monarch surrounded by beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullen and melancholy is a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: The Spanish girl has a party in the Land of Promise

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
Dora is a girl's name
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl throws a party in a fabled paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by conquistadors is a land of promised riches.

clue.text: Student gets suitable work for computer

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate, standing for a student
apt means suitable
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A learner finds the right job for a PC.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable machine used on the knees is a type of computer.

clue.text: Measures spasms appearing after operation

indicators.note: appearing after puts the spasm word behind the operation word

parts.note: tics are involuntary spasms

explanation.surface: Muscle twitches show up after surgery and are recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs, optics are the upturned bottle dispensers giving fixed measures of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub spirit dispensers that pour fixed tots are called by this name, so they are measures.

clue.text: Shop's exit

definitions.meaning: a retail store, especially a factory store

explanation.definitionFit: A retail store is a sales point, and a vent or way out is also called this.

clue.text: Plunder left for killjoy

parts.note: spoils are plunder taken in war
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Loot abandoned for a party-pooper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ruins others' fun is a killjoy.

clue.text: Gloria's heartless greeting

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter of the greeting word

parts.note: hallo is a greeting

explanation.surface: A woman called Gloria offers a cold welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloria' looks like a name, but it is a word for a ring of light round a saint's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloria is an aureole or nimbus, the radiance painted round holy figures.

clue.text: Deer's posterior

explanation.definitionFit: A female red deer bears this name, and as an adjective it means rear, as in back legs.

clue.text: Top man to kill in the US

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
to ice is American slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A boss orders a hit in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' reads as a leader; 'Top' alone is the definition, a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting upper garment of a dress is a top.

clue.text: Tiny tree ruined forever

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A small tree spoiled for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless time is a synonym, as in waiting forever.
